issues.failure_explanation: The operation count is near-quadratic only when the number of retained components stays O(log n); the source supplies no condition ensuring this at fixed tolerance. For dense orthogonal A and B, AB has all singular values equal to one. The SVD first-order output has rank at most 2k, so its relative Frobenius error is at least sqrt(1-2k/n). Achieving 1% therefore requires k proportional to n, not log n.

failure_location.quote: The proposed methods scale as $\mathcal{O}(n^2 \log n)$ in arithmetic operations for $n \times n$ matrices for usable tolerances in relative error $\sim$ 1\%.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State complexity in terms of the required truncation size, and make the O(n^2 log n) fixed-tolerance claim conditional on a suitable decomposition-tail assumption. For flat spectra, acknowledge that the SVD method requires cubic-order work.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised coupling of approximately 1% accuracy with O(n^2 log n) work does not hold over the stated general dense-matrix scope.
issues.title: Fixed-tolerance near-quadratic complexity lacks a compressibility condition
issues.why_classification: A complete correction must exclude an advertised dense-matrix regime or materially worsen the fixed-accuracy complexity guarantee.
